text: Jay was in his room, texting the home assistant on his phone. "why is the water bill so big?? i dont want tips, just the numbers," he wrote. The assistant understood that Jay wanted only this month's water use and no advice. It told him the house used nine thousand four hundred litres, up from seven thousand last month. Jay was surprised. Then he noticed that the speaker in the kitchen had gone quiet. "unmute my favourite speaker, the kitchen one," he typed. The assistant turned the sound back on in the kitchen speaker and played one short beep to show it was working. Jay said thanks and went to check the bathroom tap.

Sam was scared that his school essay was too long. He picked up his phone and typed, "hey, count the words in my essay about my old camera." The assistant opened the essay he had been writing and counted every word. It told him the essay had four hundred and twelve words. Sam's teacher had asked for three hundred, so he needed to cut about a hundred. "ok show me the last paragraph," he wrote. The assistant read the last paragraph out loud, and Sam crossed out two sentences he did not need. Then he asked for the count again. This time the assistant said three hundred and ninety words. Sam smiled and kept cutting.

On social media, a post is a photo, a video or a few words that you share with your followers. People use posts to show a trip, a new baby or a big ship they saw in the harbour. Most apps let you change a lot about how they work. You can ask the assistant to turn off notifications, hide the likes or stop videos from playing by themselves. People say things like, "stop the clips from starting on their own," or "tell me only when my sister posts." If you want to know the exact number of people who follow you, you can ask for that too.

name: check_sun_time
does: Tells a person how long they can stay in the sun before their skin gets burned, using the sun's strength and their skin type.
inputs: the beach or town, the person's skin type, and the time they plan to be outside
people say:
- How long until I burn?
- I'm heading out the door to the beach, how much time do I have?
- My shoulders were sore and red last summer, I don't want that again.
- Will I be fine if I paint the boat on the sand all morning?
- Is it too sunny for the kids at noon?
- When should I put on more cream?

Person: I need to tell the electricity company that I'm moving.
Assistant: I can help with that. What date are you leaving the old house?
Person: The movers come in the middle of next week.
Assistant: Which day exactly? Wednesday or Thursday?
Person: Thursday. Also I need twice as many boxes as I have now, and a rubber band for my garden tools.
Assistant: I can add boxes to your shopping list, but I can't buy a rubber band for you. Do you want the boxes on the list?
Person: Yes please. And remind me to clean the shed half a day before the movers arrive.
Assistant: Done. I'll remind you on Wednesday at noon.

Rosa the cook was chopping onions when the kitchen got too bright. "Make the lights half as bright," she said to the voice assistant. The assistant lowered the ceiling lights to half. A minute later Rosa said, "Now a little warmer, the way my dad's old lamp used to look." The assistant changed the colour of the bulbs to a soft yellow. Rosa wanted to find the right colour, so she scrolled through the colour list on her phone. "What is the least bright white you have?" she asked. The assistant picked the dimmest white and turned the lights to that. Rosa nodded and went back to her onions.

Ken was late. He grabbed a bar of chocolate and ran out the door, talking to his phone. "how far will i walk to the station? estimate it, i only have twenty minutes." The assistant understood that Ken wanted a guess of the distance and the time. It said the station was about one and a half miles away and the walk would take twenty-eight minutes. That was too slow, so Ken asked for a faster way. The assistant showed a shorter route through the park. Ken also asked it to add the walk to his monthly distance total. The assistant saved it and told him he had walked thirty miles so far this month.

name: read_beach_flag
does: Says what colour flag is up at a beach today and whether it is safe to swim.
inputs: the name of the beach
people say:
- Is it safe to swim today?
- Is the flag green at Long Sands?
- Are the waves too big? I don't want to wipe out.
- Can the kids go in the water?
- Did anyone put a warning up on the beach camera page?
- What do the lifeguards say about the sea right now?

name: log_pet_food
does: Writes down how much food a pet has eaten today so nobody feeds the pet twice.
inputs: the pet's name and the amount of food, in cups or ounces
people say:
- Rex just had six ounces of kibble.
- I think the cat already ate, can you check?
- Did anyone feed Milo this morning?
- Put down that I gave Luna half a cup.
- The bowl is damp and empty, was that dinner?
- How much has the dog had since breakfast?

Mr. Ortiz did not like phones much, but his grandson had set up the assistant for him. A neighbour was coming for a picnic, and the grass was long. He typed quickly, "mow teh lawn at three, picnic at four". The assistant understood that he wanted the robot mower to cut the lawn at three o'clock. It also checked the local weather and saw clouds coming at four. It told Mr. Ortiz about the rain and asked if he wanted to block the sprinklers for the day. He said yes. So the assistant started the mower for three o'clock and stopped the sprinklers until tomorrow.

Lena was texting from the bus. "Could you please turn on the sprinklers in the back garden for ten minutes? My brother is away this week and I promised him I'd look after his tomatoes, and the whole bed looks dry." The assistant understood that she wanted the back sprinklers on for ten minutes because the tomato bed was dry. It started them and said it would stop at the right time. When Lena got home, her shoes were muddy. She wiped them on the mat and went to look. The tomatoes were wet, and the leaves looked happy again.

Mr. Patel owned a small shop, and on Friday it was ten years old. "Could you please make my lemon cake recipe big enough for thirty people? I'm bringing it to the shop party and I want everyone to have a slice," he said to the kitchen assistant. The assistant understood that the recipe made six slices and that Mr. Patel needed five times as much. It listed the new amounts: ten cups of flour, ten eggs and a big bucket of batter, all in cups and spoons. Mr. Patel wanted gold sprinkles on top, so the assistant added them to his shopping list.

Priya had just come to the city and her flat was full of boxes. "I need double the tape and half as many bags," she told her phone. The assistant understood that she wanted twice the usual tape and fewer bags, so it made a list with four rolls of tape and five bags. Then she said, "Where do I put my motorcycle?" The assistant looked up parking near her street and found two places. Priya wanted a single bed, so she asked for shops that sold one. While she waited she began to peel the old tape off a box. The assistant sent her three shops near the flat.

Grandma Ruth stood in the garden and looked at her beans. "Oh dear, those poor beans look so thirsty," she said to the garden speaker. She did not say the word water, but the assistant understood what she meant. It turned on the drip hose by the bean row for fifteen minutes. Ruth hoped the leaves would stand up again. "And tell me when the next dry day is," she added. The assistant looked at the calendar and the weather and told her the next dry date was Thursday. Ruth smiled, and she asked it to remind her that morning to pick the beans.

Tom owned a small shop, and Diwali was only a week away. He wanted to fill the window with lights, but the weather was bad. "Put string lights and candles on my shopping list, and tell me if it will be stormy on Saturday," he said to his phone. The assistant understood that Tom wanted two things: add two items to his list and check the weather. It put string lights and candles on the list. Then it said Saturday would be dry, but a stormy night was coming on Sunday. Tom decided to hang the lights in the yard behind the shop on Saturday afternoon.

Most pets eat at the same times every day. A feeding schedule tells you when the dog or cat gets its food and how much. People use it so nobody forgets or feeds the pet twice. Families change the schedule when they go camping, when the vet says the pet is too heavy or when the weather is hot. You can ask an assistant for these changes in plain words. People say, "remind me to feed Max at six," or "give Luna a smaller dinner," or "fold the Sunday walk into the Saturday one." The main thing is to keep the times the same, so the pet knows when to expect its food.

Noor was getting ready for bed. She said to the smart speaker, "Wake me up at seven for school." The speaker set an alarm for seven. Then Noor remembered the weekend. "No wait, not seven, make it eight, there's no school tomorrow!" The assistant understood that she had changed her mind and fixed the alarm. It said the alarm was now for eight in the morning. Noor wanted her room to look neat, so she put her toys away. Then she asked the speaker to raise the volume of the quiet bedtime song. The assistant made the music a little louder, and Noor fell asleep.

When you have a party, the first thing you need is a guest list. It says who is coming and who is not. People send an email or a text to invite them, and they ask the assistant for help. They say things like, "send the invitation to everyone on my list," or "upload the photo of the cake to the party message." Later, many people change the list. They say, "add my cousin," or "take Dan off, he can't come." Some people print the invitation on thick paper and some only send it online. Either way, the assistant keeps a count of how many people said yes.

Dana was an office worker with a long list of jobs. In the morning she told her phone, "Organize my to-do list, put the report first and the phone calls after lunch." The assistant moved the report to the top and the calls to the afternoon. A moment later she changed her mind. "Sorry, not the report first, I need the order form done first." The assistant understood that she wanted the order form at the top. It moved the form up and put the report in second place. Dana felt steady again. At noon she checked off the form, and the assistant crossed it out of the list.

Person: Can you record the soup video and send it to my sister?
Assistant: Sure. Which video do you mean, the one from today or the one from last week?
Person: Today's, I'm cooking dinner right now.
Assistant: Got it. Do you want me to send it as soon as it ends?
Person: Yes, and also learn which clips I watch the most and put them in a little list for me.
Assistant: I can send the clip when it ends. I can't learn from your clips, but I can save the ones you pick into a list.
Person: Okay, that is fine.

Mrs. Boyd was a kind person who did not like new machines. On her April trip she stayed in a hotel, and the room was very dark. She stood by the bed and said, "I can hardly see in here, dear." The room assistant understood that she meant the lights were too low. It turned the lights up and said they were brighter now. Mrs. Boyd was happy. Later she said, "These towels are a mess," while she tried to fold one. The assistant understood that she wanted fresh towels, so it sent a message to the front desk. A new pile came to her door ten minutes later.

Mr. Hale was moving to a new town and was not good with phones. "I don't want the expensive movers," he said to the assistant. "And I don't want to pay for boxes I can't use again." The assistant understood that he wanted cheaper movers and no new boxes. It looked up three moving companies and sorted them by price. Then it found a shop that rents boxes, which you can return. Mr. Hale asked it to find a time for Saturday. The assistant showed him one company with a free spot on Saturday morning and wrote it on his calendar. He thanked it, a little amazed.

name: find_battery_hogs
does: Shows which apps are using the most battery on a phone or tablet and lets the person close them.
inputs: the device, and how far back to look, like today or this week
people say:
- Why is my battery dying so fast?
- Search for the app that is eating all my power.
- Which games drain the tablet the most?
- My phone died by lunch again, what did that?
- Close whatever is using the battery in the background.
- Will I make it to the next charge?

Yoga music was playing in the kitchen, but Miguel the cook found the room too bright. He began to chop peppers and said, "Dim the lights by half." The assistant lowered the ceiling lights to fifty percent. The kitchen still felt cold, so he said, "Make them warmer, more yellow." The assistant changed the bulbs to a warm yellow. Then he asked it to make the lamp over the stove twice as bright, because he needed to see the knife. The assistant raised only that lamp to full and left the rest dim. Miguel nodded and kept cooking.

They want to know when the baby is next due to eat.
Feeding time?
Next bottle?
When does she eat again?
What time did I last feed him?
I want to follow the baby's schedule today, when is the next meal?
How long since the creamy cereal at breakfast?
Can you tell me when to feed the baby next, I'm baking and I've got flour all over my hands?
Could you please let me know what time the next feed is, so I can put the baby down for a nap after?

Zoe was waiting for a package. She texted her phone, "where's my order? i need it by friday at noon." The assistant looked up the order and read the post tracking. It said the box was at the local depot and would be delivered on Thursday afternoon. That was the first good news Zoe had heard all week. She wanted to be sure, so she asked the assistant to scan her email for the delivery message. It found one and said the driver would come between two and four on Thursday. Zoe asked it to remind her at one o'clock on Thursday to be home. The assistant set the reminder.

name: check_printer_ink
does: Looks at a printer and tells the person how much ink is left in each colour and when it will probably run out.
inputs: the name of the printer
people say:
- Is the printer low on ink?
- Do I have enough black ink to print this year's tax papers?
- Why are my pages coming out pale?
- Touch base with the printer and tell me what it needs.
- How many pages can I print before I need new cartridges?
- Tell me if the friendly little printer in the hall is out of ink.

Mrs. Green was a retired teacher with a big lawn. She told the garden assistant, "Please start the robot mower at ten." The assistant set it for ten o'clock. Then Mrs. Green said, "Oh, wait, my grandma is visiting at ten and sitting in the garden. Make it two o'clock instead." The assistant understood that she had changed her mind and moved the start to two. It also said the mower would cut the grass in its normal pattern and finish around four. Mrs. Green then asked it to pack the mower away in its box if it started to rain. The assistant said it could send her a message in that case, but it could not pack the mower itself.

name: tidy_contacts
does: Finds people who are saved twice in the address book and joins them into one entry.
inputs: nothing, or the name of one person to check
people say:
- I have the same friend in my contacts three times.
- Organize my address book, it's a mess.
- Sorry, I added Aunt Rita twice, can you fix that?
- Clean up the doubles in my phone numbers.
- Is Mark in there more than once?
- Give me a minute and merge the extra copies.

They want a gift idea for a friend who has a birthday soon.
Gift idea?
What should I get Sam?
I need something nice for my mum, she turns fifty.
What do you think a ten-year-old would like?
I want to see some ideas for a warm jacket or something like it.
Can you find me a present for under twenty-five dollars?
My friend lives out west and likes plants, got any thoughts?
Could you please suggest something kind and not too expensive for a coworker's birthday next week?

It was September and the first cold evening. Grandpa Joe sat in the living room and breathed on his cold hands. "Please turn the heating on and make the living room twenty degrees," he told the thermostat. The assistant turned on the radiators and set the room to twenty. Then Joe said, "And bring back the warm blanket from the bedroom, dear, if you can." The assistant said it could not carry blankets. It could, however, turn on the heater in the bedroom so the room would be warm when he went back for it. Joe laughed and said that would do.

Max was a child who loved getting letters and packages. He asked the speaker in the hall, "When will my parcel come? Mum said it's a toy." The assistant looked up the order. It said a driver would deliver the parcel tomorrow at about ten in the morning. Max looked at the sharp pencil in his hand and wrote the time on a card. Then he said, "Tell me again tomorrow at nine." The assistant made a reminder for nine o'clock. The next day, at nine, the speaker said that the parcel was close, and Max ran to the door.

Mr. Wu was not good with phones, but his daughter had put an assistant on his table. His hands were shaky and the baby upstairs was crying, so he spoke very briefly. "Pills time?" he asked. The assistant understood that he wanted to know when to take his next medicine. It said he took one pill at eight in the morning and the next was due at eight tonight. Mr. Wu was worried that it was late, but the assistant said it was still normal to wait. Then he asked it to heat the milk bottle alarm. It set a timer for the baby's milk instead and told him so.

Person: It's really hot in the room where I plan to stay next weekend.
Assistant: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want a room with air conditioning?
Person: Yes please. Please find something nearby the lake.
Assistant: I can look. How many nights will you stay?
Person: Three nights, from Friday.
Assistant: Thank you. I can't book a room myself, but I can search and show you hotels near the lake with air conditioning.
Person: That would be fine. My salary doesn't go far, so show the cheap ones first.
Assistant: Sure, I'll sort them by price.

name: update_mower_schedule
does: Changes the days and times when a robot mower cuts the lawn.
inputs: the mower's name, the days, and the start and end times
people say:
- Mow only on Mondays and Thursdays.
- Can you update the mower so it stops before the kids come out?
- Don't cut the grass while the toy tractor is out there.
- Start the mower an hour earlier on Saturday.
- Check online and tell me if the mower has new settings.
- I want it to rest on rainy days.

Every computer keeps your things in files, and files live in folders. A screen shows you what is open, and a battery keeps the computer going when it is not plugged in. People change a lot of small things every day. They make the screen brighter, set it to a medium size for the text or ask the computer to restart when it gets slow. You can say these things out loud to an assistant. People say, "make the text bigger," "close all the windows," or even shout, "restart the computer!" when the machine will not work. Then they wait a minute while the glass screen goes dark and comes back.

When you buy something online, the shop packs it in a bottle or a box and gives it to a delivery driver. You can follow this trip with a tracking number. It tells you where the parcel is and when it will arrive. People use this to plan their day. If the parcel is late or wrong, they ask for a refund or a new one. They say things like, "where is my order?" or "change the delivery to Friday." They may also say, "continue to send me updates," or ask for the maximum number of updates a day. Most shops give you a few days to send something back.

show unread mail
unread emails?
any new mail?
what's in my inbox that i havent opened
show me the top of the inbox, the bottom can wait
I need to measure how much mail I missed, let me see the new ones.
Did anything come in while I was out marking grade papers?
Could you please open the messages I haven't read yet so I can catch up?

Hana, an office worker, came in on a freezing morning. The meeting room was cold and the heating was low. She did not want to flood the small room with heat, but she wanted it warm. "Warmer, please," she told the thermostat. The assistant understood that she wanted the temperature to go up. It raised the room from sixteen to twenty degrees and said that it would take about ten minutes. Hana put her coat on the chair and waited. When her team came in, the room was comfortable. She said, "Good," and the assistant kept the size of the heating the same.

Mrs. Lee had taught school for forty years, and now she liked to sit on her balcony with a cup of tea. One evening she said to the speaker, "Oh, it's a bit dark out here for writing, isn't it?" She did not say turn on the light, but the assistant understood. It turned on the lamp on the balcony. Mrs. Lee then said, "I wrote down a fancy word for my poem. Please keep it with my notes." The assistant opened her notes and saved the word, then asked if she wanted to read it back. She said yes, and the assistant read it out loud.

Mr. Adams was a retired teacher who wanted a smaller power bill. He sat in his kitchen and said, "Find out which of my machines uses the most electricity." The assistant searched the energy report from his house. It said the old freezer used the most, followed by the dryer. Mr. Adams was friendly with his neighbour, who had solar panels, so he asked, "How much sun power did my neighbour's house make?" The assistant said it could not see other people's houses. "Oh, I mean mine," Mr. Adams said, "I have no panels, silly me." The assistant understood that he wanted only his own report, and it read out the figures for the hill-side house.

Ella was a child who loved numbers. She put her bowl of cereal on the table and said to the speaker, "What is twelve plus eight, and what comes after you take five away from that?" The assistant understood that she was asking two questions. It said that twelve plus eight is twenty, and that twenty take away five is fifteen. Ella wrote both numbers in a straight line on her paper. Then she asked, "Now double the fifteen and tell me half of it." The assistant said double is thirty and half is seven and a half. Ella clapped, finished her cereal and asked for another one.

Plan my workouts
Give me a week of exercises
What should I do at the gym this week?
I want to plan three days of training, with rest days in between
Set me up with something to do inside, it's raining
Make me a plan for four days. Actually, make that five
Can you help me plan a routine with sets and reps, no wait, only sets for now?
Could you please put together a simple exercise plan for the week that I can do at home?

Old Mr. Cole was a gardener, and he had a lot on his mind. He stood by the shed and said, "It's a pity I'll forget the tomatoes again tomorrow." The assistant understood that he wanted a reminder, even though he did not say so. It asked, "Should I remind you in the morning?" He said yes. So it set a reminder for eight o'clock to check the tomatoes. Then Mr. Cole said, "I need a fast way to the garden shop, too." The assistant drew a route on his phone map, and the shop was only ten minutes by car. Mr. Cole thanked it and went inside.

Carla was a busy parent, and she had to get her son to the dentist. "Book me a ride to the dentist at three," she said to her phone. "But I can't afford the fancy cars, and I don't want a driver who plays loud music." The assistant understood that she wanted the cheapest ride, and a quiet one. It found a small, plain car for twelve dollars and noted that the driver liked a gentle, quiet trip. It asked her to confirm the pickup at her front door. Carla said yes, and the ride was booked for three o'clock.

A focus timer helps you work for a short time and then take a break. Many people work for twenty-five minutes, rest for five and then start again. The timer is useful because it keeps you from sitting too long. You can change the length of the work time, the break or the sound it makes. People say, "make my breaks ten minutes," or "don't ring the bell, just flash the red light." Some people skip the timer on Saturday because they want to blow off steam. Others say, "start the timer again," when they come back from lunch. It is a simple way to get a routine.

When you shop online, you choose what you want, pick a size and pay. Then the shop sends the order to your home. Many shops have a minimum amount you need to spend to get free delivery. If something does not fit, you can send it back and get your money returned. People change things all the time. They say, "change the size to medium," "deliver it to my work," or "lock the order so it cannot change." Sometimes the order is for a school project and needs to arrive by a certain day. In that case people ask, "can you get it here by Friday?"

Nina was a busy parent, and the kids were noisy in the car. She typed quickly on her phone, "play the silly song abuot the frog, then turn it up". The assistant understood that she wanted the children's song about a frog, and a louder sound. It found the song and started it, then raised the volume a little. The kids sang along. In the back, her son shouted that they should win the singing game. Nina grinned. "skip to the next one, the one from the carpet cleaner ad," she wrote. The assistant skipped ahead and played the next song.
